findings.endpoint: hemostasis parameters and bleeding risk (standardized extract)
findings.population: adults in 18 randomized controlled trials (1,985 participants; 87% with dementia, peripheral artery disease, or diabetes)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 randomized controlled trials (1,985 adults) found no evidence that standardized Ginkgo biloba extract increases bleeding risk on the hemostasis parameters studied.
findings.limitations: trial populations and durations may not capture rare events; the conventional caution about combining ginkgo with anticoagulants or antiplatelets rests on case reports rather than on this trial evidence

findings.endpoint: serotonin syndrome risk in combination with SSRIs (pharmacodynamic interaction)
findings.population: patients combining St John's wort with serotonergic antidepressants (case-report literature)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review of adverse effects and drug interactions documents that St John's wort inhibits serotonin reuptake and that combining it with SSRIs carries a case-report-documented risk of serotonin syndrome (mental status changes, tremor, autonomic instability, gastrointestinal upset, myalgias, restlessness) — a pharmacodynamic interaction distinct from its CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein effects staged in batch 11.
findings.limitations: case-report evidence, not incidence data; later case series most often involve sertraline and paroxetine, but the sample is too small to rank SSRIs by risk

findings.endpoint: use in pregnancy and lactation (statin-class contraindication)
findings.population: pregnant and lactating women (safety review of red yeast rice products)
findings.finding_summary: This medication-safety review states that statins — and therefore red yeast rice products, whose monacolin K is chemically identical to lovastatin — are generally contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation on the basis of teratogenicity in animal studies, with CNS and limb defects reported in newborns exposed to statins in utero; it also notes severe musculoskeletal and hepatic adverse reactions reported at monacolin intakes as low as 3 mg/day.
findings.limitations: the pregnancy contraindication is inherited from the statin class rather than from red-yeast-rice-specific human data; EFSA judged monacolins from red yeast rice a significant safety concern at 10 mg/day

findings.endpoint: serum digoxin immunoassay interference and shared cardiac target
findings.population: laboratory study (two commercial digoxin immunoassays; isolated adult rat cardiomyocytes)
findings.finding_summary: In this laboratory study, hawthorn extract interfered with the Abbott Digoxin III immunoassay but not the Roche Tina-Quant assay, and in rat cardiomyocytes both hawthorn extracts raised intracellular calcium without an additive effect alongside digoxin — suggesting binding at the same Na/K-ATPase site; the authors conclude patients receiving digoxin should avoid hawthorn.
findings.limitations: assay interference is platform-specific (falsely altered digoxin readings on one common immunoassay); the pharmacodynamic finding is from isolated rat cells, while the small human PK study staged in batch 11 found no change in digoxin levels — together they argue for clinician awareness rather than a demonstrated clinical harm
